newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products close lower on soybean slide.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products close lower on soybean slide.

text.p: A drop in soybean futures pressed CBOT soy product futures to a lower close, traders said.
They said the pressure came from good crop weather in South America and on a sharp break in wheat futures.
Soymeal was underpinned by talk China overnight bought 50,000 tonnes of U.S. soymeal, the traders said.
Soy products may have been pressured by the weekly National Oilseeds Processors Association report Monday which placed the weekly U.S. soy crush at 30.6 million bushels.
That tally as of November 27 was above trade expectations and above the previous week's crush total of 29.683 million bushels.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated at 25,000, below the 25,939 contracts traded Monday, according to the CBOT.
Soyoil futures volume was estimated at 25,000, below the 26,714 traded Monday.
Soyoil closed 0.12 to 0.27 cent per lb lower, with December down 0.18 at 22.56. Soymeal was $1.00 to $2.30 per ton lower, with December down $1.20 at $236.70.
